title: Flipping a literal negates its value
statement: Let $l$ be a literal over $n$ Boolean variables, given by a variable index and a polarity that marks it as positive or negated, and let $x \in \{\text{true},\text{false}\}^n$ be an assignment. Writing $\bar{l}$ for the literal obtained from $l$ by flipping its polarity while keeping the same variable, the value of $\bar{l}$ under $x$ is the negation of the value of $l$ under $x$; that is, $\bar{l}(x) = \lnot\, l(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: l is a literal over n variables
x is a Boolean assignment on n variables
